name: echo
description: Writes its arguments separated by a space, followed by a newline. Widely used to show the value of a variable or to write to a file with a redirection. In double quotes, variables ($HOME) are replaced; in single quotes, the text is printed as is.

options.description: Does not add a newline at the end.
Does not interpret escape sequences (the bash default).

arguments.name: TEXT
arguments.description: Text to print. Several arguments are separated by a space.

examples.explanation: Prints a message with the value of the USER variable.
In single quotes, the variable is not replaced.
Adds a line to the end of a file.
Interprets \t and \n to build a small table.
Prints the exit code of the last command (0 = success).
